newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index ends lower, hurt by A shares.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends lower, hurt by A shares.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B shares closed down sharply on Wednesday, following the domestic currency A shares, as fears over the possiblity of new crackdown measures by Beijing took their toll, brokers said.
The B share index lost 4.90 points or 2.89 percent to end at 164.48 as turnover shrank to HK$48.6 million from HK$87.3 million on Tuesday.
The B index hit the day's low of 163.06 in the afternoon before recouping some of the losses just before the market closed as selling pressure eased, brokers said.
The A share index tumbled 19.20 points or 3.94 percent to 467.63 on turnover of 8.0 billion yuan compared with Tuesday's 9.4 billion yuan.
"The sharp falls in the A share market pushed down B share prices because investors fear that any further falls will spill over into the B share market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
"But Beijing's recent measures were aimed at the A share market, so B share investors do not need to worry about it too much," the analyst said.
In the B share market, the biggest loser was Shenzhen Tellus Machinery, which lost HK$0.20, or 6.45 percent, to close at HK$2.90.
Shenzhen Energy was the poorest A share performer, plunging 1.71 yuan or 8.75 percent to 17.83 yuan.
The Shenzhen bourse said on Monday that a probe had uncovered illegal accounts opened for trading in Energy shares and it was conducting further investigations.
